answer: A farm therefore spreads across origins and pays for the distribution, while each origin still has to clear the wander quota and the raven admission check. Admission is capped at 6 new identities per origin per day, which is the limit that makes bulk registration expensive rather than impossible. Because the plume audit records the origin of every admitted key, a cluster arriving through one uplink is visible after the fact. That is 23 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
